title: Greenland Opens New Airport to Attract More Tourists
paragraphs: Greenland has opened a new international airport in the town of Ilulissat, hoping to bring in more tourists as the Arctic island looks to become independent from Denmark one day.
The first flight from Copenhagen, Denmark, arrived on October 29, carrying 169 passengers, including Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen.
Nielsen called the airport "one of the biggest investments" in Greenland's history.
Greenland, home to about 56,000 people, relies heavily on fishing. Its government hopes tourism will help diversify the economy and reduce its dependence on Denmark.
Ilulissat, known as the "City of Icebergs," is one of the island's most popular places to visit.

Sitting on Greenland's western coast, more than 550 kilometers north of the capital, Nuuk, the town is home to about 5,000 people. Visitors come to see its icebergs, take sled dog rides and go on boat trips.
Until now, travelers from other countries often had to change planes or arrive by cruise ship. There are no roads between Ilulissat and Greenland's other big towns.
Air Greenland plans to offer up to six flights a week between Copenhagen and Ilulissat during the busiest summer months, while Icelandair will also have flights from Iceland.
Another international airport opened in Nuuk in late 2024. United Airlines also began offering summer flights between Nuuk and Newark, New Jersey, in 2025.
But Greenland has yet to see the big increase in tourism it had hoped for.
International visitor numbers have increased by at least 65% since 2018, to almost 150,000 in 2024. However, tourism still made up less than 5% of Greenland's economy that year.
Some people also worry about the effects of growing tourism.
Palle Jerimiassen, a former mayor in the area, said that while tourism can bring in more money, the island must be careful as visitor numbers grow.
